prompt: Top-down still life, vertical 9:16, camera at 90 degrees over an Indian miniature painting lying flat. Full-bleed 9:16 picture edge to edge: the painted paper fills the whole frame, with no painted border, margin, ruled frame, mount, table edge, bands or panels anywhere. Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. It is the clasp close up and the authority on the sailor ring's spring gate, push-pin nub, ribbed collar and the straight one-row stone bar; take nothing else from it: no skin, neck or body. THE PIECE: A 50 cm chain, 4 mm wide, of elongated paperclip links (about 4 x 11 mm) in polished 18k gold tone. 1 thick round spring-gate sailor ring about 22 mm across (about 14 mm opening, small push-pin nub, ribbed gate collar) and 1 short straight bar about 15 mm long set with 1 row of about 9 tiny clear stones, on a jump ring. No pendant, no other stones. Must stay a sailor ring with a straight bar 0.6-0.7x the ring, never a plain donut ring, a lobster clasp, or a curved or multi-row pave bar. The bar is short and slim: end to end it is 0.6 of the sailor ring's outside diameter (about 13 mm against the 22 mm ring), never longer than 0.7 of it; it is about half as thick as the ring's tube; its 9 tiny clear stones fill it from tip to tip in one row, with no plain, textured, engraved or stippled block at either end; its one jump ring is at its outer tip. Seen from above, the bar lies across the ring's upper-left tube and its inner tip stops just short of the ring's centre. On the ring, the spring gate is a thinner tube across the top, running from the main tube's flat cut end at 11 o'clock to a short barrel collar at 1 o'clock; the chain's one plain round jump ring hangs on that barrel collar, with no other fittings; the push-pin nub is a small ball on a short stem at 3 o'clock, no wider than a third of the tube; two fine ribbed grooves circle the tube at 4 o'clock, just below the nub. Last time this went wrong, so correct it: the bar grew to 0.87 of the ring, too thick, with oversized stones and an invented stone-less end block; the gate was drawn at full tube thickness and the nub was oversized and fused into a wide ribbed band; the ring sat too low and too far right; the painted gate stood more than twice the ring's height; and the dunes under the chain were brighter than the metal. Every link, the sailor ring, the bar and both jump rings are the same polished 18k gold tone, never silver tone, white metal or rose. Exactly two chain ends in the picture: the long strand that forms the road ends at the ring's barrel collar on one jump ring; a second short strand ends at the bar's one jump ring and runs off the right edge just above the gate; no third strand, no loose jump ring, no extra chain end. LAID AS A ROAD: the chain enters at the left edge and winds in one gentle S across the middle to the right, where the sailor ring lies flat, gate collar and nub visible, the bar across it; the ring is about 19% of the frame width, its centre 41% of the way down the frame and 62% across, and its right edge, nub included, at least 14% of the frame width from the right edge, every link separate. SCALE: the frame shows about 100 mm of the painting across; the ring is 22 mm, a little bigger than a one-rupee coin, each link 4 x 11 mm; the ring rests on and overlaps the 18 mm painted gate, so the door-knocker is bigger than the door, by the old painters' rule, never bigger than about a quarter of the frame. THE PAINTING (Marwar school desert at dusk, opaque gouache on burnished wasli paper, flat colour fields, fine brushwork, visible paper fibre, perfectly flat; about 10 cm in frame; an original composition in that school's manner, never a copy of any known or museum painting): ochre and saffron dunes, a calm lilac-plum dusk sky with a few small round painted fireworks in white dots, and around the ring a small white palace gate, finials included no taller than one and a half times the ring's diameter, its plum doorway narrower than the ring, its base no lower than 48% down and its top no higher than 30% down, so the ring is the biggest thing on the gate, with a scalloped arch and closed plum doors; the ring rests on the doors exactly where a door-knocker would hang. The dunes the chain crosses are a deep dusky ochre-terracotta in soft shadow, darker than the metal, so every link's bright kicker edge is the lightest, most saturated thing on the page; the paler saffron dunes stay behind the procession. On the far (upper) side of the road only, with a clear 5 mm gap of plain dune between it and the chain, walks a riderless wedding procession painted small, every animal facing and walking toward the gate: three elephants in saffron and oxblood cloths carrying kettle-drums, drumsticks raised with nobody holding them, two plumed horses with empty saddles, lamps on poles; flat profile silhouettes in gouache with no painted eye dots; each animal shorter than two links, flat brushwork on the paper, never touching, crossing or overlapping any link. No riders, mahouts, drummers or people of any kind on or beside the animals, no water. CONTACT: a fine real shadow under every link, the bar and the ring, with a thin dark contact line wherever the metal touches the paper. LIGHT, two lights only: one large soft overhead daylight, no glare; one small hard specular kicker low from the left puts a bright edge on every link and the ring, and a white catchlight in each tiny stone. COMPOSITION: piece and shadow centred in the band from 26% to 53% of the frame height; 13-25% calm and plain for a headline; below 54% calm plain ground for type. The whole chain lies between 33% and 47% of the frame height; nothing of the piece is lower than 47% down. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark: no script, signatures, seals, stamps or inscription panels anywhere in the painting. No painted people or deities, no faces, no eyes, no eyebrows; animals only as tiny flat profile silhouettes. One product only: no other jewellery, no props.
